public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 898

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/898](https://www.erdosproblems.com/898)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Mordell_inequality)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Affine EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos898

/--
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

Conjectured by Erdős in 1932 (according to [Er82e]) and proved by Mordell soon afterwards, now
known as the Erdős-Mordell inequality.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos898.lean"]
theorem erdos_898 (A B C P L M N : ℝ²) (hABC : AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C])
    (hP : P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set ℝ²)))
    (hN : N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]) (hPN : line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction)
    (hM : M ∈ line[ℝ, B, C]) (hPM : line[ℝ, P, M].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, B, C].direction)
    (hL : L ∈ line[ℝ, C, A]) (hPL : line[ℝ, P, L].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, C, A].direction) :
    dist P A + dist P B + dist P C ≥ 2 * (dist P M + dist P N + dist P L) := by
  sorry

end Erdos898

reformulations.difference: The Lean does not say "N is where the perpendicular from P to AB meets the triangle", as the docstring and erdosproblems.com do. Instead it takes arbitrary points N, M, L satisfying `N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]` and `line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction`, and likewise M on line BC and L on line CA. These are the feet of the perpendiculars on the full side lines. In an obtuse triangle a foot can lie on a side's extension, outside the triangle.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) In a scratch file I proved that the two hypotheses force `N = orthogonalProjection line[ℝ,A,B] P`, via `coe_orthogonalProjection_eq_iff_mem` with `direction_affineSpan` and `vectorSpan_pair`. I also proved that the projection satisfies both hypotheses. So quantifying over N, M, L is the same as stating the inequality for the three feet; the case N = P is covered by the same proof. (ii) This is Erdős's own formulation in [Er82e] ("X is a point on BC and OX ⊥ BC etc."). It is also the explicit convention of the cited Wikipedia page: for obtuse triangles the perpendiculars "end on the line supporting one of the sides". The source calls the claim the Erdős–Mordell inequality, which is stated with distances to the side lines. (iii) In non-obtuse triangles every foot from an interior point lies on its side segment, so all readings agree. Take the most literal reading of "meets the triangle": the first boundary point the perpendicular ray from P toward AB reaches. The triangle lies in the closed half-plane bounded by line AB, so that point is no farther from P than the foot. The Lean inequality therefore implies that weaker version too. (iv) The linked formal proof `Erdos898.erdos_mordell` states the inequality with distances to orthogonal projections on the side lines, under ¬Collinear. I proved in Lean that it closes `type_of% @Erdos898.erdos_898`, using only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

review.notes:
No findings. `erdos_898` states the classical Erdős–Mordell inequality, as Erdős posed it in [Er82e] and as Wikipedia states it.
- Non-degenerate triangle: `AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C]`.
- P strictly inside: `P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ {A, B, C})`, the root topological interior. I checked this with pp.fullNames.
- Feet of the perpendiculars on the three side lines: uniquely determined, as proved in Lean.
- Conclusion: non-strict, with factor 2. `ℝ²` is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, so `dist` is Euclidean, not the sup metric.
- The hypotheses can be satisfied, and the statement is neither vacuous nor weaker than the source's claim.

Status: `research solved` with `formal_proof using lean4` matches erdosproblems.com ("PROVED (LEAN) — solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean") and the teorth/erdosproblems database ("proved (Lean)").

Formal-proof check:
- The linked file is pinned to Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1; this sandbox has Lean v4.33.1.
- Under this sandbox's Mathlib, one step fails: the final `convert h_angle_add using 1` in `angle_split_of_interior` leaves goals that need `EuclideanGeometry.angle` unfolded.
- After replacing that step with `unfold EuclideanGeometry.angle; exact h_angle_add` in a scratch copy, the whole file compiles. `Erdos898.erdos_mordell` then depends only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and it proves `type_of% @Erdos898.erdos_898` exactly.
- So the failure is caused by the Mathlib version difference, not a gap in the proof.
- Minor: the link uses `blob/main` rather than a commit permalink.

Docstring: it copies erdosproblems.com word for word, including "meets the triangle", which is loose for obtuse triangles; see the reformulation entry. Its dates (conjectured 1932, proved by Mordell soon after) match [Er82e] ("In 1932 I conjectured ... In 1934 this inequality was proved by L. J. Mordell"). Wikipedia gives 1935/1937 instead; the docstring follows its cited source.
